sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Oss spent a year changing its mind about how much parking in the centre should cost. In the policy note Parkeren in Oss 2025, adopted on 26 May 2025, the council aimed to bundle car parking in built facilities at the edge of the centre, direct long-stay visitors to the Bergoss and Oostwal-Oost garages, Burchtplein and a future Raadhuislaan facility, and make paid hours run until 22:00, to give the centre more room for pedestrians, cyclists and greenery [0]. The tariff structure in the note was 2 euros an hour with a 6-euro day maximum in the garages and at Burchtplein and Raadhuishof, and 2 euros for the first hour and then 4 euros an hour on other streets [1]. A local broadcaster reported in September 2025 that the change would apply from 1 October 2025, and that more than 200 residents reacted indignantly [4]. After the uproar the alderman announced a 12-euro daily maximum for the surface lots from 1 November 2025, still to pass the college and the council [5]. Centre traders then started a signature campaign in January 2026, one of them saying he lost 18 percent of turnover in three months; these are traders' statements [7]. On 3 June 2026 the municipality proposed to partly reverse the increase [8], and the council adopted the 2026-II ordinance on 25 June 2026, valid from 1 October 2026. Paid parking runs Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 20:00, the listed surface lots cost 2 euros an hour up to 6 euros a day, listed centre streets 2 euros an hour, and other locations in the centre and fringe 2 euros for the first hour and then 4 euros [9]. A resident permit costs 75 euros for the first and 150 euros for the second. Permit zones A to H and J are capped, for example zone A at 190 permits for 247 spaces, and residents in zones A and B get at most one permit per address and only without private parking [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The big question is the next garage. The 2025 note assumes, for its financial calculations, an above-ground garage of a rounded 700 spaces behind the town hall, shared by the theatre, visitors, residents and workers, with the municipality planning to co-invest and operate; in the longer term Burchtplein could become a built facility and Koornstraat guarded bicycle parking. These are plans [13]. The June 2026 proposal postponed a guarded bicycle garage at Eikenboomgaard, improvements at Oostwal-Oost and a future lot at Burchtplein because of lower parking revenue, and described the financing of the new Raadhuiskwartier garage as a challenge, though funding agreements were said to exist for the Lievekamp expansion and the redesign of Raadhuislaan and Lievekamplaan [14]. Around the station the note foresees an upgraded regional mobility hub, lower parking norms for new housing and the option of paid parking with permits in a wider area, where new residents would not get street permits [15]. The municipal charging vision says Oss needs 1,365 public charging points by 2030 against about 340 when written, for an expected 13,573 electric vehicles, and in principle leaves fast chargers to the market [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipal Parkeerbedrijf, a closed, cost-covering account since 1994, runs paid parking, permits, guarded bicycle parking and the garages. Street parking and the Jurgensplein lot are profitable and cross-subsidise the loss-making bicycle parking and the Bergoss and Oostwal-Oost garages [2]. The Bergoss garage opened in September 2009, and the Oostwal-Oost deck is in shared ownership with ImmoPartners Beheer [12]. The garages charge round the clock, every day, while the Rusheuvel lot north of the centre stays free, and parking is by licence plate [11]. The municipality's own assessment is that there are ample spaces on weekdays, that pressure is highest on Saturdays and during events, and that the Bergoss and Oostwal-Oost garages almost always have free spaces except during the kermis [3]. The centre management organisation puts the number of central spaces at 1,349 in October 2025, down 15.4 percent from 1,594 in 2022, including about 200 unused spaces at Maasvallei, which is its own account and not an official count [6]. Q-Park runs P+R Gasstraat, with 246 spaces and a discount for train travellers; its tariffs did not load [16].

Our data cover that park-and-ride, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 27% on weekdays and 14% at weekends, and it reached nearly full in single readings, on a Saturday afternoon among others. The garages and lots in the centre are not in our data.
